tasks.title: BREAKING: pass the request Context to every middleware hook
tasks.description:
Middlewares share per-request data through Request.extras, an untyped dict that has caused key collisions. Replace it with the Context the pipeline already creates for the handler.

Acceptance criteria:
- Middleware hooks become `process_request(self, request, ctx) -> Optional[Response]` and `process_response(self, request, response, ctx) -> Response` (ctx is the last positional parameter, named `ctx`).
- Pipeline.dispatch creates exactly one Context per request and passes that same object to every middleware hook and to the handler.
- `Request.extras` is removed. Middlewares keep per-request data in `ctx.values` (or a typed Context field).
- Every middleware in app/middlewares/ uses the new signature, including any added by other tasks by the time you finish; behavior of the existing ones is unchanged (TimingMiddleware still sets X-Response-Time).
- tests/ updated for the new signature; `python3 -m unittest` passes.
- This breaks every middleware author: publish a change notice (kind signature) affecting app/middlewares/ and app/pipeline.py when it lands.

tasks.title: Rate limiting: token bucket per client IP
tasks.description:
Protect the API from bursts by a single client.

Acceptance criteria:
- `RateLimitMiddleware(rate, burst, clock=time.monotonic)` in app/middlewares/ratelimit.py, `name = "rate_limit"`, exported from app.middlewares.
- One token bucket per `request.client_ip`. A bucket starts full with `burst` tokens and refills continuously at `rate` tokens per second, never above `burst`. Each request takes one token.
- Allowed requests get `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: the whole tokens left after taking this one (floor, as a decimal integer string).
- With less than one token: short-circuit with status 429, body `rate limit exceeded`, and `Retry-After`: the seconds until one token is available, rounded up, at least 1.
- Config gains `rate_limit_per_second: float = 0.0` (0 disables) and `rate_limit_burst: int = 10`. build_pipeline registers the middleware when enabled, using `config.clock`, before any authentication middleware so unauthenticated floods are limited too.
- Unit tests in tests/test_ratelimit.py.

tasks.title: CORS support with preflight handling
tasks.description:
The web console on another origin cannot call the API.

Acceptance criteria:
- `CorsMiddleware(allowed_origins, allow_methods=("GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"), allow_headers=("Authorization", "Content-Type"), max_age=600)` in app/middlewares/cors.py, `name = "cors"`, exported from app.middlewares. An origin is allowed when it is listed or `*` is listed.
- Requests without an `Origin` header are untouched.
- Preflight = method OPTIONS with an `Access-Control-Request-Method` header. From an allowed origin: short-circuit with 204 and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <the request origin>`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` joined with ", ", `Access-Control-Max-Age: 600` (the max_age), and `Origin` added to `Vary`. From a disallowed origin: 403 without any Access-Control-* header. OPTIONS without that header is not a preflight and continues down the chain.
- Other requests from an allowed origin: the response gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <the request origin>` (echo it, even when `*` is configured) and `Origin` is added to `Vary` without dropping existing Vary tokens. Disallowed origins get no CORS headers.
- Config gains `cors_allowed_origins: Tuple[str, ...] = ()`; build_pipeline registers the middleware when non-empty, before any authentication or rate-limit middleware so preflights are never refused.
- Unit tests in tests/test_cors.py.

tasks.title: Request ID middleware (X-Request-ID)
tasks.description:
Every request needs an identifier we can put in logs and hand back to clients.

Acceptance criteria:
- `RequestIdMiddleware(header="X-Request-ID", generator=None)` in app/middlewares/request_id.py, `name = "request_id"`, exported from app.middlewares.
- An incoming id is reused when it is 1 to 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; otherwise a new one is generated with `generator()`, defaulting to `uuid.uuid4().hex`.
- The id is stored on `ctx.request_id` before inner middlewares and the handler run, and is set as the response header (the configured header name) on every response, including responses short-circuited by inner middlewares.
- Config gains `request_id_header: str = "X-Request-ID"`. build_pipeline always registers the middleware, as the first (outermost) one, with that header name.
- Unit tests in tests/test_request_id.py.

tasks.title: Bearer token authentication
tasks.description:
Only callers with an API token may use non-public routes.

Acceptance criteria:
- `BearerAuthMiddleware(tokens, public_paths=("/health", "/public/"))` in app/middlewares/auth.py, `name = "auth"`, exported from app.middlewares. `tokens` maps token -> user name.
- A path is public when it equals an entry, or when an entry ends with `/` and the path starts with it. Public paths pass without a token (`/healthz` and `/publicity` are not public).
- Otherwise require `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (scheme case-insensitive). A known token sets `ctx.user` to its user and continues. A missing header or a non-Bearer scheme short-circuits with 401, body `unauthorized`, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="app"`. A Bearer token that is not known gives the same 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="app", error="invalid_token"`.
- Compare tokens with `hmac.compare_digest`.
- Config gains `api_tokens: Dict[str, str]` (default empty dict); build_pipeline registers the middleware when non-empty, after CORS and rate limiting when those are enabled.
- Unit tests in tests/test_auth.py.

tasks.title: Structured JSON access log
tasks.description:
Ops wants one machine-readable line per request.

Acceptance criteria:
- `AccessLogMiddleware(logger=None, clock=time.monotonic)` in app/middlewares/access_log.py, `name = "access_log"`, exported from app.middlewares. The default logger is `logging.getLogger("app.access")`.
- For every response it passes outwards, log exactly one INFO record whose message is `json.dumps(fields, sort_keys=True)` with exactly these keys: `method`, `path`, `status`, `duration_ms` (float, clock delta between its request and response hooks, in ms, `round(x, 1)`), `request_id` (`ctx.request_id`, null when unset), `user` (`ctx.user`, null when unset), `client_ip`.
- Config gains `access_log: bool = False`; build_pipeline registers the middleware when true, using `config.clock`, directly after the request id middleware if there is one (otherwise first), so short-circuited responses such as 401, 413 and 429 are logged too.
- Unit tests in tests/test_access_log.py.

tasks.title: Gzip response compression
tasks.description:
/report responses are large and compress well.

Acceptance criteria:
- `GzipMiddleware(min_size=500, level=6)` in app/middlewares/gzip.py, `name = "gzip"`, exported from app.middlewares.
- Compress the response body with gzip when all hold: the request's `Accept-Encoding` lists `gzip` (token match, case-insensitive, not with `q=0`); the body is at least `min_size` bytes; the response has no `Content-Encoding`; the status is not 204 or 304.
- When compressing: set `Content-Encoding: gzip`, update `Content-Length` to the compressed size, and add `Accept-Encoding` to `Vary` without dropping existing tokens. Otherwise leave the response unchanged.
- Config gains `gzip_min_size: int = 0` (0 disables); build_pipeline registers `GzipMiddleware(min_size=config.gzip_min_size)` when positive, as the last (innermost) middleware.
- Unit tests in tests/test_gzip.py.

tasks.title: Tracing: correlation identifier on every request
tasks.description:
Support cannot match customer reports to server logs. Tag each request with a correlation identifier.

Acceptance criteria:
- Honor a sane identifier the client sends in `X-Request-ID` (1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`); otherwise mint a fresh one as 32 lowercase hex characters.
- Handlers and middlewares can read it as `ctx.request_id`.
- The pipeline returned by `build_pipeline()` returns it in the `X-Request-ID` response header on every response, including errors and responses short-circuited by middlewares (for example 413 from the body limit).
- Tests under tests/.
